title: Yuka, the preserved juvenile mammoth carcass
summary: In August 2010 an almost fully intact juvenile woolly mammoth carcass, nicknamed Yuka, was found in permafrost on the Oyogos Yar coast of Yakutia, with brain, flesh, skin and fur preserved. Its age is given as about 35,000 years by radiocarbon work at Novosibirsk State University but as 39,000 years by Guinness World Records. Cuts on the carcass may have been made by ancient hunters.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree: about 35,000 years (radiocarbon, Novosibirsk State University; "34-35 kyr BP"), 39,000 years (Guinness World Records), and "about thirty-eight thousand" (AFP via NBC News). Years ago are counted from the present, rounded to -37000 to -32000; no calibration is stated.

as_recorded.value: preserved for about 35,000 years (according to the radiocarbon analysis)
In August 2010, the almost fully intact carcass of a 39,000-year-old female juvenile woolly mammoth
